_: Swimwear fabric: warp-knit (tricot / raschel) polyamide with elastane ~80/20 by mass, 170-220 g/m2, 0.5-0.66 mm, four-way stretch, usually cut double (self-lined) for cups. Mass, thickness and loop density are measured on commercial swim knits (SWIM24, S1 S2 S3 S7). Its tensile curves exist only as figures (SWIM25), so stretch, bending and shear are scaled from the nearest tabulated stretch knit (JOVANOVIC22 WE17, a plated weft knit for compression wear) by areal mass and thickness and marked E. Optics, thermal and states start as fabric.nylon_elastane's (the same fibres; E). fs-cloth lane, 11-11.

alpha.src: smooth filament knit with a soft sheen; no BRDF fit retrieved

n.src: E: recalled from Morton & Hearle 2008 (MORTON08), not re-read: nylon mean 1.551 (MORTON08 recalled)

sheen.v: noticeable, follows the wale direction; stretched areas thin out and let the colour beneath show (lighter / more transparent over curves)

fibre_n.src: E: recalled from Morton & Hearle 2008 (MORTON08), not re-read: MORTON08 nylon 6,6 1.582 / 1.519 (recalled; the brief's 1.53 / 1.58); elastane ~1.5 nearly isotropic (E)

stretch_whitening.v: opacity falls with strain: areal cover ~1/(1+e_x)(1+e_y)
stretch_whitening.src: mass conservation of the knit (fibre area constant while the cell grows)

wet_darkening.src: LEKNER88 / Angstrom film model, diffuse light; the index-matching effect inside the yarn (ZHANG06) darkens further and is not in this formula; white thin fabric also turns translucent (fibre/water index ratio ~1.16 instead of ~1.55 in air)

static.src: compliant knit, high real contact area; fabric band 0.2-0.6

surface_energy_mJ_m2.src: E: recalled from textbook / trade ranges, not re-read: nylon 6,6 ~46 (recalled)

moisture_regain_pct.src: ASTMD1909 nylon 4.5 (M); elastane 1.3 (E, not retrieved); mass-weighted 0.8 x 4.5 + 0.2 x 1.3

v.position: positive (nylon among the most positive fabrics)

surface_resistivity_ohm_sq.src: E: recalled from Morton & Hearle 2008 (MORTON08), not re-read: MORTON08 order; nylon varies widely with history and additives (lecture copy of Hearle, via search)

abrasion.src: TYPICAL: nylon is the most abrasion-resistant common fibre; elastane is attacked by chlorine and body oils over time

collision_thickness_mm.src: half of T0 1.23 mm at 0.5 gf/cm2 (T0 1.23 mm M (JOVANOVIC22 WE17); Tm, LC, RC typical knit, E; RT taken as 1 - HYI wale 0.477; inputs E)

contact_stiffness_kPa_per_mm.src: KES-FB3 secant: (4.903 - 0.049) kPa / (T0 1.23 - Tm 0.85) mm (T0 1.23 mm M (JOVANOVIC22 WE17); Tm, LC, RC typical knit, E; RT taken as 1 - HYI wale 0.477; inputs E)

initial_stiffness_kPa_per_mm.src: secant x LC 0.35: LC < 1 means the pile is soft first then stiffens as fibres pack

compressible_to_fraction.src: Tm / T0 at 50 gf/cm2 (~5 kPa, a firm press or sitting); beyond it the fibres themselves resist (fibre modulus, GPa)

penetration_response.ramp_note: stiffening ramp (LC < 1): IPC log barrier starting at collision_thickness, or a two-slope ramp initial -> secant

contact_damping_ratio.src: (1 - RC 45 %) / (4 pi): energy lost per press-release cycle; RC from T0 1.23 mm M (JOVANOVIC22 WE17); Tm, LC, RC typical knit, E; RT taken as 1 - HYI wale 0.477

restitution.src: a cloth layer dropped or slapped on a rigid flat does not bounce: energy goes into bending and fibre friction (no measurement found)

response_time_ms.src: a cloth flap / slap reads as a short damped crack; set by the in-plane wave crossing a ~0.3 m panel at the speeds below plus bending

wave_speed_m_s.src: sqrt(stretch_N_m 175 / mass 0.28 kg/m2) and sqrt(shear_N_m_rad 22.5 / mass); transverse (flutter) speed is sqrt(tension / mass) and depends on load

min_separation_mm.src: two half-thicknesses: folded layers rest T0 apart at light pressure, Tm under ~5 kPa

skin_friction_note.src: TEMEL22: cotton single jersey on living chest skin (2 N, 0.04 m/s), the nearest knit-on-skin measurement; a pair row for this fabric is not yet in pairs/

density_kg_m3.src: SWIM24: apparent, mean g/m2 / mean mm

fibre_density_kg_m3.src: E: recalled from Morton & Hearle 2008 (MORTON08), not re-read: MORTON08 (recalled)

areal_density_g_m2.src: SWIM24 Table 1, S1 S2 S3 S7 (78-80 % PA / 20-22 % EL); garment = their mean

thickness_mm.src: SWIM24 Table 1 (EN ISO 5084 at 1 kPa), S1 S2 S3 S7; garment = their mean

elastic_limit_pct.src: JOVANOVIC22 WE17 point T (above it the knit takes permanent set)

secant_stiffness_N_m.src: elastic_limit_force_N_m / elastic_limit strain: ~100x softer than woven cotton

curve.v: J-shaped: soft loop-straightening to ~the elastic limit, then yarn extension stiffens it ~10-30x toward break
curve.src: break force / elastic-limit force ~33-44x over ~3.5x the strain (JOVANOVIC22)

hysteresis_index.src: JOVANOVIC22 WE17 HYI (energy lost / loading energy)

nylon_only_elastic_limit_pct.src: JOVANOVIC22 NE (0 % elastane): elastane is what extends the elastic range

bending_rigidity_gfcm2_cm.src: fine-gauge knit; knit B ranges 0.002-0.05 (cotton-knit patent via search)

shear_rigidity_N_m_deg.src: knit low end (0.3-1.2 cotton knit range via search)

poisson.src: knits neck down strongly when stretched one way (loop geometry); not measured here

recovery.v: elastic snap-back below the elastic limit; slow creep recovery of the rest over minutes to hours; repeated over-stretch bags out (knees)

sim._: Stretch warp knit: two-branch (J) membrane as fabric.nylon_elastane, at the swim knits' measured mass and thickness. The low branch is E (scaled); replace it with a measured tricot curve when one is tabulated.

stretch_N_m.src: JOVANOVIC22 WE17 secant (175 / 179 N/m) scaled by areal mass 0.691 (SWIM24 mean / 280); the tricots measured in SWIM25 are given only as figures

compression_garment_pressure_kPa.v: P = T / r (Laplace): T 100 N/m over a 50 mm-radius thigh -> 2 kPa (15 mmHg)
compression_garment_pressure_kPa.src: a check a sim of leggings on skin should reproduce

wet_strength_ratio.src: by definition: wet / dry strength ratio, the conditioned dry strength (20 C, 65 % RH) is the reference

loop_density_per_10mm.src: SWIM25 Table 3, horizontal / vertical loops per 10 mm before ageing

heat_capacity_J_kgK.src: E: recalled from textbook / trade ranges, not re-read: nylon ~1.7 kJ/kgK (recalled)

melt_C.src: E: recalled from textbook / trade ranges, not re-read: recalled

stretched_on_body.src: a worn legging sits at 20-60 % strain: inside the low branch, opacity reduced (optics_summary.stretch_whitening)

deform.fracture.wet_strength_ratio.src: nylon carries the load: COTTONINC13 nylon dry 2.3-5.0, wet 1.8-4.0 gf/den (0.78-0.80; row checked by density 1.14 / regain 4.5) and NYLON2 80-90 %; spandex dry 0.5-1.5 = wet 0.5-1.5 (ratio ~1.0, COTTONINC13) so the elastane share does not lower it

wet.src: E: recalled from Morton & Hearle 2008 (MORTON08), not re-read: ~40 % water; nylon loses ~10-15 % strength wet (MORTON08 recalled); wet swimwear clings and darkens

JOVANOVIC22.cite: Jovanovic T, Penava Z, Vrljicak Z. Impact of the elastane percentage on the elastic properties of knitted fabrics under cyclic loading. Materials 15(19):6512 (2022). doi:10.3390/ma15196512. Plated weft knits, 156 dtex polyamide ground + wrapped (WE) or bare (CE) elastane

ASTMD1909.cite: ASTM D1909-13(2020)e1 Standard tables of commercial moisture regains for textile fibres (cotton 8.5, wool 13.6, silk 11, flax 12, nylon 4.5, polyester 0.4 %); read through a CC BY review table citing it (Bioresour Bioprocess 2020, 10.1186/s40643-020-00339-1 Table 10) and the ASTM catalogue abstracts. Commercial (agreed) regains, close to equilibrium at 65 % RH, 21 C
ASTMD1909.lic: paywalled standard; the numbers are facts

KRUSS228.cite: KRUSS application report AR228: single-fibre Wilhelmy contact angle, nylon 6.6 in water 76.6 +/- 4.1 deg
KRUSS228.lic: free application note, (c) KRUSS; number used as a fact

LEKNER88.cite: Lekner J, Dorf MC. Why some things are darker when wet. Appl Opt 27(7):1278-1280 (1988): a water film's total internal reflection returns diffuse light to an absorbing surface for another chance of absorption (Angstrom), plus a lower relative index inside
LEKNER88.lic: paywalled journal; author copy; formula used, text studied only

ZHANG06.cite: Zhang H, Voss KJ. Bidirectional reflectance study on dry, wet and submerged particulate layers: effects of pore liquid refractive index and translucent particle concentrations. Appl Opt 45 (2006): index matching lets light go deeper and be absorbed; neither model alone sufficient
ZHANG06.lic: paywalled journal; author copy; studied only

MORTON08.cite: Morton WE, Hearle JWS. Physical Properties of Textile Fibres, 4th ed. Woodhead (2008): fibre densities, refractive indices, moduli, wet/dry strength, electrical resistance. Recalled; not re-opened in this session
MORTON08.lic: copyrighted book; individual numbers as facts; recalled, so marked E

ALPHALAB.cite: AlphaLab Inc. (W. Lee) triboelectric table, charge affinity nC/J at ~22 C, 35 % RH (2009); cotton +5, wool 0 read from secondary copies (blog / Scribd); nylon listed with dry skin at +30
ALPHALAB.lic: (c) AlphaLab, may be reproduced only whole; single numbers used as facts, table not copied

UNITS.cite: Unit conversions done here: 1 gf = 9.80665 mN; KES B gf cm2/cm x 98.07 = uN m per unit width; KES G gf/(cm deg) x 56.19 = N/m per rad; KES-FB1 standard max load 500 gf/cm = 490.3 N/m; 1 oz/yd2 = 33.906 g/m2; 1 momme = 4.306 g/m2; 1 ft3/ft2/min (ASTM D737, 125 Pa) = 5.08 mm/s

TYPICAL.cite: Trade and textbook typical values (fabric weight classes, Martindale rating bands such as EN 14465 upholstery 'heavy domestic' >= 25 000 rubs, fabric emissivity ~0.9, effective fabric conductivity dominated by trapped air 0.03-0.06 W/mK). Used only where no measured value was retrieved; each use says why

COTTONINC13.cite: Textile Fibers (2013), Cotton Incorporated: cotton is 10-20 % stronger when wet (dry 3.0-4.9, wet 3.3-6.7 gf/den in the text); appendix 'Comparison of fiber properties' dry / wet tenacity gf/den: cotton 3.0-5.0 / 3.3-6.0, flax 5.5-6.5 / 6.0-7.8, silk 2.4-5.1 / 2.0-4.3, nylon 2.3-5.0 / 1.8-4.0, spandex 0.5-1.5 / 0.5-1.5 (rows identified by density and regain: the PDF text layer shifts the row labels by one)
COTTONINC13.lic: (c) 2013 Cotton Incorporated, all rights reserved: text STUDY ONLY (P13); a few numbers used as facts

NYLON2.cite: Secondary textile notes (Scribd 'Nylon 6,6' manufacturing notes; mytextilenotes): nylon wet strength 80-90 % of dry, elongation +5-30 % wet; no primary source named
NYLON2.lic: unverified secondary; used as a supporting range only

SWIM24.cite: Potocic Matkovic VM, Salopek Cubric I et al. The Impact of Chlorinated Water and Sun Exposure on the Durability and Performance of Swimwear Materials. Polymers 16 (2024) 3050

SWIM25.cite: Gabriela, Potocic Matkovic VM, Salopek Cubric I. Seawater and Sunlight as Critical Ageing Factors Affecting the Mechanical Performance of Knitted Swimwear Fabrics. Materials 18 (2025) 5346

TEMEL22.cite: Temel, Johnson, Lloyd. Evaluating the Repeatability of Friction Coefficient Measurements and Tactile Perceptions in Skin-Textile Interactions. Tribology Letters (2022)
